advances:
The common-source overflow has the exact allocation
\[
\left|\frac{P+A_2}{2}\cap\{f_j>0\}\right|
=E+\rho,
\]
where
\[
\rho=
\left|
\bigl(D_R\cap\{f_j>0\}\bigr)
\setminus(D_i\cup D_\ell)
\right|.
\]
Thus only the part of the simultaneous-low midpoint body not already
covered by the two side midpoint bodies can absorb overflow. At the
exact calibration,
\[
E+\rho\ge
\frac{20\sqrt{97}-167}{1600}.
\]
This replaces the unbounded rectangle proxy in accepted fact
`7d5ee83bd565a34f` by one actual overlap residual. Aggregating all
high-sign endpoint cell-pair inclusions gives explicit cap-allocation
bounds for its three sign sectors. Those scalar bounds do not make
\(\rho\) smaller than the overflow threshold, so the remaining task is
precisely to control this uncovered absorption using common-plane shape.
author: mp_r93_regime_a_common_source_allocation
proof:
All cutting lines have planar area zero. The closed cells in (4) cover
\(A_2\), including every zero-cell boundary. Minkowski addition
distributes over a finite union, so
\[
U:=\frac{P+A_2}{2}
=D_Q\cup D_i\cup D_\ell\cup D_R.
\tag{23}
\]
For \(z=(x+y)/2\in D_Q\), equations (2)-(4) give
\[
f_i(z)\ge0,\qquad f_\ell(z)\ge0,\qquad f_j(z)\le-1.
\]
Thus \(D_Q\cap\{f_j>0\}=\varnothing\).

If \(z\in D_i\cap\{f_j>0\}\), then \(f_\ell(z)\ge0\), and (2) forces
\[
f_i(z)=-1-f_\ell(z)-f_j(z)<0.
\]
Similarly,
\[
D_\ell\cap\{f_j>0\}\subseteq\{f_i\ge0,\ f_\ell<0\}.
\]
The two sets in (7) are therefore disjoint. Removing from
\(D_R\cap\{f_j>0\}\) the points already covered by them gives the
disjoint union
\[
U\cap\{f_j>0\}
=
\bigl(D_i\cap\{f_j>0\}\bigr)
\mathbin{\dot\cup}
\bigl(D_\ell\cap\{f_j>0\}\bigr)
\mathbin{\dot\cup}
\mathcal R.
\tag{24}
\]
This proves the equality in (9), with no assumption about overlaps
among \(D_i,D_\ell,D_R\).

By (1), \(U\subseteq K\), so
\[
|U\cap\{f_j\le0\}|\le c_j.
\]
Planar Brunn--Minkowski gives
\[
|U|\ge\frac14(\sqrt p+\sqrt r)^2.
\]
Subtracting the first inequality from the second and using (24) proves
the inequality in (9). This is the global-overflow step underlying
accepted fact `7d5ee83bd565a34f`, re-derived here without its rectangle
relaxation.

For the cap allocation, the two endpoint halfspace intersections in
(10) are compact convex sets of areas
\[
p+x_i,\qquad q+b_i.
\]
They are unions, up to null cutting lines, of the four source-target
pairs
\[
(P,Q),\quad(P,B_i),\quad(X_i,Q),\quad(X_i,B_i).
\]
Every corresponding midpoint has \(f_\ell\ge0\). Compatibility and
Brunn--Minkowski therefore give
\[
G_\ell\subseteq K\cap\{f_\ell\ge0\},
\qquad
|G_\ell|\ge
\frac14\left(
\sqrt{p+x_i}+\sqrt{q+b_i}
\right)^2.
\tag{25}
\]
The analogous four high-\(i\) cell pairs give
\[
G_i\subseteq K\cap\{f_i\ge0\},
\qquad
|G_i|\ge
\frac14\left(
\sqrt{p+x_\ell}+\sqrt{q+b_\ell}
\right)^2.
\tag{26}
\]
In Alternative 1, \(p,q>0\), so both applications remain valid even
if one of \(B_i,B_\ell,X_i,X_\ell\) has zero area.

The sets \(G_\ell\) and \(\mathcal R_i\setminus G_\ell\) are disjoint
subsets of \(K\cap\{f_\ell\ge0\}\), whose area is \(s-c_\ell\).
Consequently
\[
|\mathcal R_i|
\le s-c_\ell-|G_\ell|+\theta_i.
\]
Together with (25), this is the first inequality in (14). The second
follows identically from (26).

Every point of \(K\cap\{f_j>0\}\) lies in at least one of the two caps
\(\{f_i\le0\}\), \(\{f_\ell\le0\}\), by (2). Hence
\[
\left|
\bigl(K\cap\{f_i\le0\}\bigr)
\cup
\bigl(K\cap\{f_\ell\le0\}\bigr)
\right|
\ge s-c_j.
\]
Inclusion-exclusion gives
\[
\left|
K\cap\{f_i\le0,\ f_\ell\le0\}
\right|
\le c_i+c_\ell-s+c_j.
\]
Since \(\mathcal R_{i\ell}\) is contained in this intersection, the
third inequality in (14) follows. Adding the three inequalities in
(14) proves (15).

Substitution of (16) gives
\[
p+x_i=p+x_\ell=\frac{197}{200},
\qquad
q+b_i=q+b_\ell=\frac{41}{800},
\]
and direct expansion gives (17). Also
\[
c_i+c_\ell-s+c_j=\frac{517}{2000}.
\]
Equations (18)-(21) now follow from (9), (14), and (15).

Finally, the determinant-one stress family does not invalidate these
inequalities. If the same determinant-one linear map \(S\) is applied
to both endpoint bodies, then every common-source midpoint body becomes
\[
D_Y^{\,S}=S(D_Y).
\]
Thus all its areas remain fixed. If the affine forms are pulled back,
every set and overlap in (7)-(15) has exactly the same area. If the
forms are instead held fixed, the sign portions can move, but
\[
0\le\rho\le|D_R^{\,S}|=|D_R|,
\]
whereas a product of normal depth and tangential width can diverge.
The proof above uses actual unions, intersections, and cap areas, never
that rectangle product, so it survives both versions of the affine
stress. Empty \(R,B_i,B_\ell\) cells merely delete their corresponding
midpoint bodies from (23)-(24).
statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2,K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact convex bodies with
nonempty interiors, and assume
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq K.
\tag{1}
\]
Let \(f_i,f_\ell,f_j\) be nonconstant affine functions satisfying
\[
f_i+f_\ell+f_j=-1,
\tag{2}
\]
and let \(a_i,a_\ell\in\mathbb R\). Use the closed endpoint cells
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
P=A_0\cap\{f_i\ge a_i,\ f_\ell\ge a_\ell\},&
X_i=A_0\cap\{f_i\le a_i,\ f_\ell\ge a_\ell\},\\
X_\ell=A_0\cap\{f_i\ge a_i,\ f_\ell\le a_\ell\},&
Z=A_0\cap\{f_i\le a_i,\ f_\ell\le a_\ell\},
\end{array}
\tag{3}
\]
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
Q=A_2\cap\{f_i\ge-a_i,\ f_\ell\ge-a_\ell\},&
B_i=A_2\cap\{f_i\le-a_i,\ f_\ell\ge-a_\ell\},\\
B_\ell=A_2\cap\{f_i\ge-a_i,\ f_\ell\le-a_\ell\},&
R=A_2\cap\{f_i\le-a_i,\ f_\ell\le-a_\ell\}.
\end{array}
\tag{4}
\]
Put
\[
\begin{gathered}
p=|P|,\quad x_i=|X_i|,\quad x_\ell=|X_\ell|,
\quad q=|Q|,\quad b_i=|B_i|,\quad b_\ell=|B_\ell|,\\
r=|A_2|,\qquad s=|K|,\qquad
c_h=|K\cap\{f_h\le0\}|\quad(h=i,\ell,j),
\end{gathered}
\tag{5}
\]
and define
\[
D_Q=\frac{P+Q}{2},\qquad
D_i=\frac{P+B_i}{2},\qquad
D_\ell=\frac{P+B_\ell}{2},\qquad
D_R=\frac{P+R}{2}.
\tag{6}
\]
An empty cell has an empty midpoint body. Let
\[
E=|D_i\cap\{f_j>0\}|+
|D_\ell\cap\{f_j>0\}|,
\tag{7}
\]
\[
\mathcal R=
\bigl(D_R\cap\{f_j>0\}\bigr)\setminus(D_i\cup D_\ell),
\qquad
\rho=|\mathcal R|.
\tag{8}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
E+\rho
=
\left|\frac{P+A_2}{2}\cap\{f_j>0\}\right|
\ge
\frac14(\sqrt p+\sqrt r)^2-c_j.
}
\tag{9}
\]

There is also a cap allocation using all four high-\(\ell\) cell-pair
midpoint bodies and all four high-\(i\) cell-pair midpoint bodies. Put
\[
G_\ell=
\frac{
\bigl(A_0\cap\{f_\ell\ge a_\ell\}\bigr)
+
\bigl(A_2\cap\{f_\ell\ge-a_\ell\}\bigr)
}{2},
\tag{10}
\]
\[
G_i=
\frac{
\bigl(A_0\cap\{f_i\ge a_i\}\bigr)
+
\bigl(A_2\cap\{f_i\ge-a_i\}\bigr)
}{2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Partition \(\mathcal R\), up to cutting lines of area zero, as
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal R_i&=\mathcal R\cap\{f_i\le0,\ f_\ell>0\},\\
\mathcal R_\ell&=\mathcal R\cap\{f_i>0,\ f_\ell\le0\},\\
\mathcal R_{i\ell}&=\mathcal R\cap\{f_i\le0,\ f_\ell\le0\},
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
and set
\[
\theta_i=|\mathcal R_i\cap G_\ell|,
\qquad
\theta_\ell=|\mathcal R_\ell\cap G_i|,
\qquad
\Theta=\theta_i+\theta_\ell.
\tag{13}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
|\mathcal R_i|
&\le
s-c_\ell
-\frac14\left(
\sqrt{p+x_i}+\sqrt{q+b_i}
\right)^2
+\theta_i,\\
|\mathcal R_\ell|
&\le
s-c_i
-\frac14\left(
\sqrt{p+x_\ell}+\sqrt{q+b_\ell}
\right)^2
+\theta_\ell,\\
|\mathcal R_{i\ell}|
&\le c_i+c_\ell-s+c_j,
\end{aligned}
}
\tag{14}
\]
and consequently
\[
\boxed{
\rho\le
s+c_j
-\frac14\left(
\sqrt{p+x_i}+\sqrt{q+b_i}
\right)^2
-\frac14\left(
\sqrt{p+x_\ell}+\sqrt{q+b_\ell}
\right)^2
+\Theta.
}
\tag{15}
\]

For the exact rational calibration
\[
\begin{gathered}
p=\frac{97}{100},\quad
x_i=x_\ell=\frac3{200},\quad
q=\frac9{200},\quad
b_i=b_\ell=\frac1{160},\\
r=\frac1{16},\quad
s=\frac{47}{50},\quad
c_i=c_\ell=\frac{209}{500},\quad
c_j=\frac{29}{80},
\end{gathered}
\tag{16}
\]
put
\[
G_*=
\frac14\left(
\sqrt{\frac{197}{200}}+\sqrt{\frac{41}{800}}
\right)^2
=\frac{829+4\sqrt{8077}}{3200}.
\tag{17}
\]
Equations (9), (14), and (15) become
\[
E+\rho\ge
\frac{20\sqrt{97}-167}{1600},
\tag{18}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\mathcal R_i|
&\le\frac{261}{500}-G_*+\theta_i,\\
|\mathcal R_\ell|
&\le\frac{261}{500}-G_*+\theta_\ell,
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
\[
|\mathcal R_{i\ell}|\le\frac{517}{2000},
\tag{20}
\]
\[
\rho\le
\frac{1255-4\sqrt{8077}}{1600}+\Theta.
\tag{21}
\]
This scalar cap bound alone is much larger than the overflow threshold:
\[
\frac{1255-4\sqrt{8077}}{1600}
>
\frac{895}{1600}
>
\frac{20\sqrt{97}-167}{1600},
\]
using \(\sqrt{8077}<90\) and \(\sqrt{97}<10\).
In particular, (18) forces a positive exclusive side charge whenever
\[
\rho<
\frac{20\sqrt{97}-167}{1600}.
\tag{22}
\]
